text: Left due to food shortage
A resident shouldered a pack and left. Food has been gone for too long.
The storehouse has food to spare, and there is dry wood by the hearth. People have started calling this place a settlement. The craftworkers suggest clearing out a workshop.
Everyone has a role, and things are running smoothly. You can now switch between 1× and 2× speed as you like.
An old surveyor from the underground storehouse has moved to the settlement with two apprentices. He still remembers the old city's street numbers.
The injured resident has recovered and returned to work.
Wandering residents arrive
Two scavengers followed the cooking smoke here. Their packs are empty, and they're willing to stay and work.
A wanderer walks into the settlement and asks if there's an empty bed.
More hands, and more mouths to feed. Residents receive rations every 10 seconds; build a hunting lodge to assign people to hunting full-time.
Convoy contract shared equally

One pot for all
Scavengers wait outside the storehouse. The workers are watching. How should the food in the pot be shared?
Equal shares: Rations and output stay at normal levels. Tighten: Save one quarter of rations; output drops by one tenth. Generous: Add one quarter to rations; output rises by one tenth.
Cutting rations erodes trust. Wait 120 seconds after each vote before changing the policy again.
Old transit station
A freight schedule for the Earth-Mars route still hangs on the waiting room wall. The last sailing was never cancelled.
You recognize the old shipping codes on the schedule. People bound for Mars used to board here. On the back of an old maintenance diagram, someone marked a pumping station.
Bring back records and parts
Returned with a route map to the pumping station and 24 scrap. The faded page still lists “Mars” as the destination.
The rusted pumping station
Water leaks through cracked pipes into the ground. The electrical cabinet is dead, but the mechanical bypass still moves.
The repair crew connected the water filter pipes using the workshop's prototype notes. Supplies must be left there and people sent regularly to keep the water flowing.
Engage the mechanical bypass
The wheel is turning again. The settlement can establish a supply outpost along the old pipeline.
Empty platform
Pry off the metal fittings that are still intact. Only the wind answers from the end of the tracks.
Collect the parts
Returned with 8 scrap.
Caravan from the river valley
The caravan leader spots the pumping station plans and asks to use the road you've repaired to transport goods.
They'll trade scrap for food. Letting them through could bring lasting trade, but you don't yet have the strength to secure the entire route.
Allow mutual transit
The river valley caravan has noted the settlement's location. Later, you can trade food for parts at the crossroads.
Keep it closed for now
The caravan left a marker by the old highway. You can contact them again whenever you're ready.
Public storage maintenance in this city
The cold night wind

The windbreaks at this city's public storage need urgent repairs, and routine maintenance wasn't scheduled this cycle. You can spend wood to replace them now, or free up production workers for one cycle to reinforce them first.
